_comment: Per-chain network and asset parameters. Checked in deliberately: none of it is secret, and a single typed registry is what makes Certus multi-chain rather than one-chain-at-a-time. Secrets stay in .env. Every chainId here was verified live with `cast chain-id`; every token pair came from a live POST /query_deposit_atoken_list. Nothing in this file is from memory.
_eligibility: hackathonEligible reflects the Cleanverse Build announcement: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon, Avalanche, BNB Chain, Monad. Arbitrum and Avalanche are eligible but Cleanverse returned NO A-Token pairs for them, so they are not usable. Base is usable but NOT eligible, so it must not carry the submission.

monad.label: Monad Testnet
monad.notes: Origin token is Circle FiatToken v2, so USDC comes from faucet.circle.com (Monad Testnet), not the Cleanverse faucet whose reservoir here is empty. Funded and ready.

selfIssuedAToken.note: Certus-issued A-Token. All four pipeline checks verified against it. Unlike aUSDC we control its institutional whitelist, which is the only route to real A-Token settlement.

polygon.label: Polygon Amoy
polygon.notes: Second Circle-faucet chain, so the natural pair with Monad for a cross-chain demo. rpc-amoy.polygon.technology was unreachable from here; publicnode works.

bsc.label: BNB Smart Chain Testnet
bsc.notes: WARNING: 18 decimals and a DIFFERENT aToken address from the other chains. Any code that assumes 6dp or a single canonical aToken is wrong here. Not funded.

ethereum.label: Ethereum Sepolia (assumed)
ethereum.notes: UNCONFIRMED which network Cleanverse means by 'ethereum'. Sepolia is an assumption, not a verified fact: confirm the origin token exists at that address on Sepolia before deploying. Sepolia gas is also scarce.

base.label: Base Sepolia
base.notes: NOT hackathon-eligible. Retained only because the escrow was first proven here and it is a useful low-cost test chain. The submission must not depend on it.
